  {"company": "Google", "use": "Android platform components (Bluetooth, keystore, networking, etc.)", "source": "https://security.googleblog.com/2021/04/rust-in-android-platform.html"},

  {"company": "npm, Inc.", "use": "Authorization service in the registry's production path", "source": "https://www.rust-lang.org/static/pdfs/Rust-npm-Whitepaper.pdf"},
  {"company": "Tilde", "use": "Skylight, the Rails profiler's agent and backend", "source": "https://www.rust-lang.org/static/pdfs/Rust-Tilde-Whitepaper.pdf"},
  {"company": "Embark Studios", "use": "Game development tooling and projects (rust-gpu and others)", "source": "https://www.embark-studios.com/"},
  {"company": "Oxide Computer", "use": "Hubris embedded OS and rack-server firmware", "source": "https://github.com/oxidecomputer/hubris"},
  {"company": "Parity Technologies", "use": "Polkadot SDK, the blockchain node software", "source": "https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk"},
  {"company": "Solana Labs", "use": "Solana blockchain validator", "source": "https://github.com/solana-labs/solana"},
  {"company": "InfluxData", "use": "InfluxDB 3 time-series database engine", "source": "https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb"},

- **Verification:** I checked the links with an HTTP request. Most returned 200, but I couldn't confirm the Microsoft and Mozilla pages and the GitHub repo links, because the server returned 403 to my automated request. I believe all of them are real, but I haven't confirmed what the Microsoft and Mozilla pages say. Open those in a browser to confirm.
- **GitHub sources:** These are company-maintained repos. They show the company ships Rust, but they aren't blog posts that say "we use Rust in production."
- **Meta:** It appears twice, as two separate sources. Dropping the second entry leaves 29 companies. Adding another would restore 30.
- **Date:** I haven't checked whether any of these companies have changed course since the sources were published. Several are from 2017–2022.
